newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Down on prompt offers, ample supply.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Down on prompt offers, ample supply.

text.p: Ample supplies, prompt offers and poor buying interest caused prices in the high sulphur fuel oil market to dip $1 on Monday and traders expected prices to gradually ease after their rise last week.
The 180-cst was traded at $101 per tonne for delivery April 19-23, compared with $102.5 traded on Friday also for mid-April lifting, traders said.
Amid prompt offers, suppliers were forced to lower their prices. The 180-cst grade was offered earlier between $101.50 and $102.50 per tonne for April lifting.
A big local trading company pushed the physical market up last week following its aggressive gas oil buying spree in the past three weeks.
The move was aided by strong crude values and swaps, pushing trading level for the 180-cst grade to as high as $104 at one stage, but the upward momentum failed to sustain.
"Most people are watching what the local trader will do next after prices fell on ample supplies," said one trader.
"He has to be careful if he wants to continue pricing," the trader said. "Once he bids, someone may just sells because supplies are very sufficient now," said one trader.

Residual fuel stocks in Singapore are also high, putting pressure on prices further. Latest figures showed that stocks for the week ending March 19 rose by 932,000-tonnes to 11.76 million barrels after a 2.1-million build in the previous week.
Sentiment was also dampened by arbitrage cargoes, estimated at about 250,000 tonnes from the Mediterranean since the beginning of March, and lower swaps quotes, they said.
April fuel oil swaps weakened to $98.00/$99.00 from $99.50/$100.50 on Friday. May swaps were at $97.00/$98.50 against $98.50/$99.50.
In the LSWR market, traders were bearish on Indonesia's April allocation, expected sometime this week.
They said Pertamina was due to make an initial alocation of 3.6 million barrels - lower than March's volume of 3.7 million barrels.
A rollover of 600,000 unsold March barrels and an additional 400,000 barrels could also be expected as later allocation, bringing the total to 4.6 million barrels, they said.

Regional demand is unlikely to absorb the volume, with only half a million barrels going to South Korea's KEPCO while Japan is only likely to take 1.0 million as the alternative burning crudes were much cheaper, they said.
"LSWR prices are still pretty high here and with so much supplies at this moment, trading interest is very very low," said one trader.
